facts.statement: The genus Titanonarke was described by Carvalho in 2010.
Titanonarke lived during the Ypresian age of the Eocene epoch.
facts.quote: Titanonarke is an extinct genus of large electric rays known from the Ypresian age of the Eocene epoch.

facts.statement: Two species, T. molini and T. megapterygia, are known from the Bolca Lagerstatte in Italy.
facts.quote: It currently contains two species from the Bolca Lagerstatte of Italy, T. molini and T. megapterygia.

facts.statement: Exceptional preservation of multiple whole individuals allowed scientists to reconstruct the lives of these rays.
facts.quote: The exceptional preservation of multiple entire individuals has allowed a detailed reconstruction of their lives.

facts.statement: Fossils include specimens with various life stages and preserved parasitic isopods.
facts.quote: Specimens of both species have been found with various ontogenetic stages and with parasitic isopods preserved.

facts.statement: A fossilized embryo found in one specimen indicates that Titanonarke was viviparous.
facts.quote: One specimen contains a fossilized embryo, showing this species to be viviparous.

facts.statement: Titanonarke likely inhabited shallow waters near coral reefs, similar to its modern relatives.
facts.quote: This species seems to prefer shallow water habitats associated with coral reefs, not unlike modern relatives.

facts.statement: Stomach contents show that Titanonarke ate an extinct large benthic foraminifera genus called Alveolina.
facts.quote: Stomach contents reveal a diet which included an extinct large benthic foraminifera genus, Alveolina.

facts.statement: Titanonarke belongs to the family Narcinidae.
Titanonarke is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Titanonarke lived between 56 and 48.07 million years ago during the Ypresian.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)
